title: External filed accounts are assessment evidence, not native ledger truth
summary: Civic/Companies House accounts enter Accounting through a normalized evidence contract and an AccountingAssessmentBook. They can be assessed, reconciled and compared with internal books, but they never become native GL journals merely because they were filed publicly.
invariants: Civic owns retrieval, exact source bytes, filing identity, parsing, taxonomy/context/dimension resolution and versioned mapping.
Accounting owns projection validation, evidence/mapping identity retention, assessment import and the prohibition on implicit GL conversion.
An external filed-accounts import never posts to the native AccountingBook implicitly.
Exact lexical fact evidence, normalized values, source pointers and completeness/omission evidence should survive import.
A statement intentionally not delivered is evidence of omission, not a zero.
Assessment arithmetic can verify relationships among filed facts without claiming audit assurance or reconstructing transactions that were never filed.

provenance.claim: Civic owns retrieval/parsing/mapping evidence while Accounting owns assessment import and prevents implicit conversion to native GL truth.
Real filing qualification preserves omission semantics and exact evidence without inventing unfiled figures.
